title: Kunneth for cohomology with closed support
statement:
Let $k$ be the algebraically closed field of
[def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and an integer $n\geq1$, put
$A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, and let $Z\subset X,W\subset Y$
be closed subschemes of
separated finite-type
$k$-schemes.
Let $K\in D^b(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and
$L\in D^b(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ be
bounded complexes,
with $L$ of
finite Tor amplitude.
Then the supported
exterior product is an isomorphism:

$$
\kappa^{Z,W}_{K,L}:
R\Gamma_Z(X,K)\otimes_A^LR\Gamma_W(Y,L)
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
R\Gamma_{Z\times W}(X\times_kY,K\boxtimes_A^L L).
$$

Here $R\Gamma_Z,R\Gamma_W$ are the
derived support functors.
The assertion also holds for the pro-etale realizations of these
complexes equipped with
etale-origin witnesses.

proof.text: Put $U=X\setminus Z$, $V=Y\setminus W$, and $F=p_X^*K\otimes_A^Lp_Y^*L$. The opens $U,V$ are separated of finite type: the Noetherian-space assertion for finite-type schemes in [def-weil-constructible-subset] says every subset is retrocompact, so each open meets each affine chart in a quasi-compact open. Choose finite basic-open covers of these intersections inside a finite affine cover of $X$ or $Y$. If a chart has coordinate ring $B$ finitely generated over $k$, each basic open has coordinate ring $B_f$, generated by those generators together with $f^{-1}$. Thus these finitely many charts prove finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The diagonal of an open subscheme is the restriction of the original closed diagonal to the open product, hence is again closed, proving separatedness by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For later application of comparison to $P=X\times_kY$, its products of affine charts have coordinate rings $B\otimes_kC$, generated over $k$ by the finitely many generators $b_i\otimes1$ and $1\otimes c_j$; these finitely many charts prove that $P$ is of finite type. After reordering the factors of $P\times_kP$, its diagonal is the product of the two closed diagonals; on affine charts its defining ideal is the sum of their extended defining ideals, so it is closed. Thus $P$ is separated as well. Choose $c$ with $H^i(K)=0$ for $i<c$ and $a,b$ bounding the Tor amplitude of $L$. For any representative $P$ of $K$, replace it by its good truncation: zero in degrees below $c$, $\operatorname{coker}(d_P^{c-1})$ in degree $c$, and $P^i$ in degrees $i>c$. Its cohomology is that of $K$, so it is a representative zero below $c$. By [lem-kun-0f1m], $L$ has a K-flat representative $Q$ with flat terms and $Q^i=0$ for $i<a$, and its final clause preserves these properties under termwise module pullback $u^*Q=u^{-1}Q\otimes_{u^{-1}A_Y}A_T$. For each projection or open immersion here, clause (1) of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] identifies $u^{-1}A_Y$ with $A_T$, and clause (2) identifies this module pullback with the exact inverse image. Thus the current ringed-site formulation of [lem-kun-0f1m] applies to these constant-coefficient pullbacks. Exactness of module inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] means $p_X^*K$ is still represented in degrees at least $c$. Thus $p_X^*K\otimes_Ap_Y^*Q$ represents $F$ and its degree $r$ term is zero for $r<c+a$: there are no summands with indices $i\geq c,j\geq a,i+j=r$. The same degree calculation after open restriction proves all complexes on $U\times Y$, $X\times V$, and $U\times V$ used below are bounded below. This verifies the bounded-below hypotheses of the support triangles without imposing constructibility or any flatness on $K$.

source.place: Proof paragraph 1, first two sentences; boundedness of every product and restriction

proof.text:
For the support pair $W\subset Y$, [lem-pur-support-restriction-triangle] with $B=Y,C=W$ gives the triangle $R\Gamma_W(Y,L)\to R\Gamma(Y,L)\to R\Gamma(V,L|_V)\to R\Gamma_W(Y,L)[1]$. Tensor it on the left with $R\Gamma(X,K)$; this is distinguished by [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] with $R=A$, using the symmetric tensor identification. Compare with the support triangle for $X\times W\subset X\times Y$, whose complement is $X\times V$. By [lem-pur-supported-product-localization] in the second variable, the supported product $\kappa^{X,W}_{K,L}$ and the two ordinary exterior products form a morphism of these triangles, including the last square. The ordinary products for $(X,Y)$ and $(X,V)$ are isomorphisms by [lem-pur-ordinary-kunneth-finite-ring], which explicitly states invertibility of the canonical Kunneth arrow in the ordinary unbounded small etale $A$-module derived categories. Our bounded complexes and their open restrictions are objects of those categories, and $\ell\neq\operatorname{char}(k)$ is part of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]; $V$ is separated of finite type by the chart argument in step 1. Therefore [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] shows that the actual supported product
$$R\Gamma(X,K)\otimes_A^LR\Gamma_W(Y,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_{X\times W}(X\times Y,F)$$
is an isomorphism. For full support, sections with support are all sections, so $\kappa^{X,Y}$ is the ordinary product by [def-pur-supported-exterior-product].

Perform the preceding construction with $U$ in place of $X$ and $K|_U$ in place of $K$. The open $U$ is a separated finite-type $k$-scheme; the boundedness requirements were verified in step 1. The support triangles [lem-pur-support-restriction-triangle] and the exact tensor functor [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] therefore apply. The morphism of triangles supplied by [lem-pur-supported-product-localization] has ordinary products on $(U,Y)$ and $(U,V)$ as its second and third components, which are the full-support ordinary products by [def-pur-supported-exterior-product] and are isomorphisms by [lem-pur-ordinary-kunneth-finite-ring]. By [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] its first component is the isomorphism
$$\kappa^{U,W}_{K|_U,L}:R\Gamma(U,K|_U)\otimes_A^LR\Gamma_W(Y,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_{U\times W}(U\times Y,F|_{U\times Y}).$$
The first components in steps 2 and 3 are the specified exterior products, rather than unspecified completions of two commuting squares.

Now use [lem-pur-support-restriction-triangle] for $(X,B=X,C=Z,K)$ and tensor with $R\Gamma_W(Y,L)$. The resulting row is distinguished by [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor]. The target row is [lem-pur-support-restriction-triangle] for $T=X\times Y$, $B=X\times W$, $C=Z\times Y$. Its first support is $(X\times W)\cap(Z\times Y)=Z\times W$ and its third term is $R\Gamma_{U\times W}(U\times Y,F|_{U\times Y})$; in particular its third ambient scheme is $U\times Y$. Apply [lem-pur-supported-product-localization] in the first variable, with its $B=X,C=Z,D=W$. Its three components are precisely $\kappa^{Z,W}_{K,L}$, $\kappa^{X,W}_{K,L}$ and $\kappa^{U,W}_{K|_U,L}$, with the shift identification at the boundary. The second and third are isomorphisms by steps 2 and 3, so [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] proves that $\kappa^{Z,W}_{K,L}$ is an isomorphism. Its identity as the map in [def-pur-supported-exterior-product] is part of the cited localization compatibility, not an appeal to uniqueness of triangle completion.

For the pro-etale realizations first take the canonical witnesses $(K,1)$ and $(L,1)$. Use [lem-pur-support-site-comparison] for $(X,Z,K)$, $(Y,W,L)$ and $(P=X\times Y,Z\times W,F)$; step 1 guarantees its bounded-below hypotheses. In the notation of that node, its equality says
$$\kappa^{Z,W}_{\nu_X^*K,\nu_Y^*L}=(R\Gamma_{Z\times W}(\theta)\circ c^{Z\times W}_{P,F})\circ\kappa^{Z,W}_{K,L}\circ(c^Z_{X,K}\otimes_A^Lc^W_{Y,L})^{-1}.$$
All factors on the right are isomorphisms by that comparison lemma and step 4; a functor, here the derived tensor bifunctor, preserves isomorphisms and their inverses. For specified witnesses $\alpha:\nu_X^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}K_p$ and $\beta:\nu_Y^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}L_p$ as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], the derived pairing has the following naturality equation:
$$
\kappa^{Z,W}_{K_p,L_p}\circ(R\Gamma_Z(\alpha)\otimes_A^LR\Gamma_W(\beta))
=R\Gamma_{Z\times W}(\alpha\boxtimes_A^L\beta)\circ\kappa^{Z,W}_{\nu_X^*K,\nu_Y^*L}.
$$
Indeed, on supported sections the two composites both send $s\otimes t$ to $p_X^*\alpha(s)\otimes p_Y^*\beta(t)$: pullback and tensor are functors. On cochain representatives the section pairings commute degreewise with coefficient chain maps and their differentials. This equality survives localization at quasi-isomorphisms in the K-flat tensor and injective support constructions of [def-pur-supported-exterior-product] and [lem-pur-support-site-comparison]: a derived coefficient morphism is represented by a roof, and the equality for its numerator and denominator gives the displayed equality for the roof. Solving this equation for $\kappa^{Z,W}_{K_p,L_p}$ expresses it as the proved isomorphism conjugated by $R\Gamma_Z(\alpha)\otimes_A^LR\Gamma_W(\beta)$ and $R\Gamma_{Z\times W}(\alpha\boxtimes_A^L\beta)$, both isomorphisms. Hence the assertion holds for the given realizations with their actual witnesses, in the ordinary finite-ring module-sheaf categories.
